subject: Predict number of individuals per occasion

messages.author: c9764e156c059aac
messages.subject: Predict number of individuals per occasion
parts:
Hello Unmarked group

We are using N-mixture models for a slightly different purpose than usual. We want to estimate a given species predicted number of individuals in different eras based on findings from archaeological sites. Our "site" is an era and "occasions" are spatial replicates-  sampled sites.  

We were able to predict the number of individuals in each era and predict detection in each sampled site, but we wanted to know if there's a way to predict the number of individuals in a specific sampling occasion (in our case site). 

Thank you,

Hila Shamoon

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Predict number of individuals per occasion
parts: As traditionally performed, the N-mixture assumes that N is constant at a specific site for all occasions.  But there are some alternative formulations for single-visit N mixtures (Subhash Lele and Peter Solymos, I think) or dynamic N-mixture models that allow inference about N to made with a single visit (Dail and Madsen 2011, see pcountOpen in unmarked); another alternative might be to use something like a time-of-removal sort of approach (multinomial N-mixture, see gmultmix or multinomPois in unmarked).
